text.what: An eye, drawn or moulded, worn where another person will see it. It is the most widespread sign in this atlas and the only one whose logic is stated out loud by its carriers everywhere it appears: harm arrives by looking, so the answer looks back.
text.story:
Amulets against a harmful look have been found dating to around five thousand years ago, and the belief runs through the Mediterranean, the Balkans, Eastern Europe, West Asia, Central Asia, South Asia, Africa, the Caribbean and Latin America. Jewish rabbinic literature returns to it repeatedly.

The sign takes two different bodies. In Egypt it is a drawn eye with a falcon's cheek-line, cut in faience and carnelian from the Old Kingdom onward. Around the eastern Mediterranean it becomes a bead: after glass-bead production got going in the region around 1500 BCE, blue-and-white concentric eye beads spread among Phoenicians, Persians, Greeks, Romans, Arabs and Ottomans, and that bead is what a shop in Istanbul or Athens sells today.

What is striking is what stands in for the eye where the eye is not drawn. Illyrians used shapes of the phallus, the hand, the leg and animal teeth against the same harm. Romans used the fascinum, a winged phallus. Southern Italy still cuts a horn. *Inference —* the substitutions have one thing in common: each is a thing that catches a glance. The mechanism carriers describe is interception, and anything startling enough to take a look can do the job. That is why this atlas files the horn, the hand and the fist as kin of the eye rather than as unrelated signs.

*Tradition holds —* the harm is usually attributed to envy, and often to admiration that has not been qualified. That is why the eye is put on children, on livestock and on new houses more than on anything else.

against_facts.label: The evil eye

material_facts.label: Faience
material_facts.note: glazed quartz paste; Egypt's amulet material at scale

material_facts.label: Carnelian
material_facts.note: red; Egypt's colour for blood and life

kin_in.name: Cimaruta
kin_in.as: the harm this charm is aimed at, stated in its own language as mal'occhio
kin_in.name_th: ชีมารูตา (กิ่งต้นรูเครื่องรางอิตาลี)

kin_in.name: Cornicello
kin_in.as: the harm it answers; southern Italy substitutes a horn where the eastern Mediterranean draws an eye
kin_in.name_th: คอร์นิเชลโล (เขานำโชคอิตาลี)

kin_in.name: Cowrie strand
kin_in.as: the sign one modern ethnographic author reads in the shell's slit underside — an attribution the source makes and this atlas repeats as an attribution
kin_in.name_th: สายเปลือกหอยเบี้ย

kin_in.name: Dzi bead
kin_in.as: the sign counted on its surface — an eye here is a circle, and the number of them sets the price
kin_in.name_th: หินดีซี (ลูกปัดทิเบต)

kin_in.name: Ethiopian talismanic scroll
kin_in.as: the sign painted on it in geometric pairs, rimmed in red, against the harm that arrives by looking
kin_in.name_th: คัมภีร์ม้วนเครื่องรางเอธิโอเปีย (คิตาบ)

kin_in.name: Evil eye bracelet
kin_in.as: the sign, and the reason a factory bead and a hand-blown one make the same claim
kin_in.name_th: สร้อยข้อมือนาซาร์ (ลูกปัดตากันตาร้าย)

kin_in.name: Fascinum
kin_in.as: the thing it is aimed at, and on the Leptis Magna and Hadrian's Wall reliefs, literally
kin_in.name_th: ฟัสซินุม (เครื่องรางรูปองคชาตโรมัน)

kin_in.name: Figa
kin_in.as: the sign this substitutes for — something startling enough to take a look
kin_in.name_th: ฟีกา (กำปั้นกันภัย)

kin_in.name: Gorgoneion
kin_in.as: the sign underneath this one; the gorgoneion's whole force sits in the glare, and Homer describes the eyes before anything else
kin_in.name_th: กอร์โกเนออน (ศีรษะกอร์กอน)

kin_in.name: Hagstone
kin_in.as: the family this atlas files a hole-you-look-through beside — though no source in this record says the hagstone is an eye, and this record does not say it either
kin_in.name_th: หินรู (แฮกสโตน)

kin_in.name: Hamsa
kin_in.as: the sign usually set in the palm; two charms stacked on one piece of silver
kin_in.name_th: ฮัมซา (มือกันภัย)

kin_in.name: Nazar
kin_in.as: the sign, in the form most of the world now buys it in
kin_in.name_th: เครื่องรางนาซาร์ (ลูกปัดตาสีฟ้า)

kin_in.name: Nimbu mirchi
kin_in.as: the harm it answers, though not the method — this string does not look back, it spoils the look
kin_in.name_th: นิมบู มีร์ชี (มะนาวกับพริก)

kin_in.name: Ojo de venado
kin_in.as: the sign this seed already is without anybody cutting it — a dark band on a pale ground, read as a pupil
kin_in.name_th: โอโฮ เด เวนาโด (ตากวาง)

kin_in.name: Tama
kin_in.as: one of the shapes stamped on them, here meaning an eye that hurts rather than an eye that looks
kin_in.name_th: ทามา (แผ่นโลหะถวายของกรีก)

kin_in.name: Wedjat eye
kin_in.as: the sign this amulet carries, and the oldest dated member of the family that runs from here to a glass bead in Istanbul
kin_in.name_th: ตาเวดจัต (ดวงตาแห่งฮอรัส)

kin_in.name: Greek and Roman protective magic
kin_in.as: the sign the whole practice is organised around, whether it is drawn or substituted for
kin_in.name_th: เวทมนตร์ป้องกันภัยของกรีกและโรมัน

kin_in.name: The square hole
kin_in.as: the square hole is called an eye in Chinese, which is a pun and not this atlas's eye family
kin_in.name_th: รูสี่เหลี่ยม

kin_in.name: The crescent
kin_in.as: the harm Roman amulets were worn against, this one included
kin_in.name_th: พระจันทร์เสี้ยว

kin_in.name: The fig fist
kin_in.as: the harm all of this is aimed at — the fist is one of the shapes that takes the look
kin_in.name_th: กำปั้นฟิก (มาโนฟิกา)

kin_in.name: The hand
kin_in.as: the sign usually set in this one's palm; two answers to the same harm stacked on one object
kin_in.name_th: มือ

kin_in.name: The horn
kin_in.as: the harm it is aimed at, and the sign it stands in for in southern Italy
kin_in.name_th: เขา (คอร์นิเชลโล)

kin_in.name: The mirror
kin_in.as: the other sign whose stated mechanism is sending a look back where it came from
kin_in.name_th: กระจก

kin_in.name: The open palm
kin_in.as: the sign set in this palm more often than any other
kin_in.name_th: ฝ่ามือเปิด (ฮัมซา)

kin_in.name: The phallus
kin_in.as: the harm it is aimed at, and in Roman art the thing it is drawn attacking
kin_in.name_th: สัญลักษณ์รูปลึงค์
kin_in.as_th: ภัยที่มันเล็งไป และในศิลปะโรมันคือสิ่งที่มันถูกวาดว่ากำลังโจมตี

kin_in.name: The beetle
kin_in.as: the other sign Egypt made by the thousand; the eye went over the incision, the beetle at the heart
kin_in.name_th: ด้วง (สคารับ)

kin_in.name: The serpent
kin_in.as: the other sign that is both the harm and the answer to it
kin_in.name_th: งู
kin_in.as_th: เครื่องหมายอีกอย่างที่เป็นทั้งภัยและทางแก้ภัยนั้น

kin_in.name: The tooth and the claw
kin_in.as: Illyrians used animal teeth against the same harm the eye is aimed at, in the same substitution set
kin_in.name_th: เขี้ยวเล็บ

kin_in.name: Glass
kin_in.as: the sign glass carries better than any other material, because a dot of colour set in a dot of colour is what glass does easily
kin_in.name_th: แก้ว

kin_in.name: Seed and nut
kin_in.as: the sign in the name: rudra-aksha, the eye of Rudra, and in Mexico the eye of a deer
kin_in.name_th: เมล็ดพืชและลูกเปลือกแข็ง

kin_in.name: The Grand Bazaar
kin_in.as: the sign under the glass — the same interception the Nile cut in faience, four thousand years later
kin_in.name_th: แกรนด์บาซาร์ (คาปาลึชาร์ชึ)

kin_in.name: Mercado de Sonora
kin_in.as: the harm the seed answers, named in Spanish as mal de ojo and stocked here by the tray
kin_in.name_th: ตลาดโซโนรา (เมร์กาโด เด โซโนรา)

kin_in.name: Monastiraki
kin_in.as: the sign itself, in a city whose writers were describing the harmful look 2,400 years ago
kin_in.name_th: โมนาสติรากิ

kin_in.name: Alan Dundes
kin_in.as: the sign his 1992 casebook assembled the arguments about, from a dozen scholars at once
kin_in.name_th: อลัน ดันดีส

kin_in.name: Frederick Thomas Elworthy
kin_in.as: the sign he catalogued across Europe in 1895, and the reason many of these objects are grouped together at all
kin_in.name_th: เฟรเดอริก โทมัส เอลเวิร์ที

kin_in.name: Siegfried Seligmann
kin_in.as: the sign his two 1910 volumes chased through every language he could read
kin_in.name_th: ซีกฟรีด เซลิกมันน์

kin_in.name: nazar
kin_in.as: the sign the word is about, and the one thing every language in its range agrees on
kin_in.name_th: นาซาร์

kin_in.name: The drawn signs
kin_in.as: the first glyph in the set, and the one the whole drawing style was settled on
kin_in.name_th: ภาพสัญลักษณ์ลายเส้น

kin_in.name: Most of them are for children
kin_in.as: the sign behind most of this class — harm arrives by an admiring look, and the admired thing is usually somebody's child
kin_in.name_th: ส่วนใหญ่ทำเพื่อเด็ก

kin_in.name: The eye everywhere
kin_in.as: the sign this read follows, and the record that holds its physical forms
kin_in.name_th: ดวงตาทุกหนแห่ง
